budget_allocation.status: ESTIMATE — no stage below is measured except parse_cavlc

parse_cavlc_full.reasoning: Current first-MB-only parse is 3 cycles/MB. Full MB parsing (mb_type, CBP, per-block CAVLC for up to 24 blocks in I420, Intra_16x16 Plane mode, I_PCM passthrough) will be much higher. CAVLC is fundamentally serial — each coefficient depends on the previous — and complex MBs at low QP can have 16 non-zero coefficients per block × 24 blocks. 50 cycles/MB provides headroom for content-dependent worst cases.

dequant_idct.reasoning: 24 blocks/MB (16Y + 4Cb + 4Cr). Currently combinational for one block. Production pipeline must clock through all 24 blocks sequentially. At 2 cycles/block (dequant + IDCT in a 2-stage pipeline): 48 cycles. The current combinational h264_dequant4x4/h264_idct4x4 modules work at 20 MHz for single-block use but will need registered outputs when processing all blocks.

intra_pred.reasoning: DC mode is trivial (~1 cycle/block) but directional modes (Vert, Horiz, DDL, DDR, VR, HD, VL, HU) need neighbor sample reads. Intra_16x16 Plane mode is a 16x16-sample computation with per-pixel multiply-accumulate. I_PCM is 384 raw bytes (bypass). Averaged across a realistic I-frame with mixed modes: ~30 cycles/MB. P-frames with inter-coded MBs skip this for most MBs.

mc_interpolation.reasoning: THE DOMINANT COST. Quarter-pel luma needs a 9x9 reference window per 4x4 sub-block (6-tap filter: 5 extra samples). For P_L0_16x16, that is a 21x21 = 441-sample reference window. DDR reference fetch: 441 luma + 162 chroma = 603 bytes. At 8 bytes/beat with alignment overhead: ~100 DDR beats. Each beat has arbitration latency (arbiter shares with frame_store display reads). Interpolation compute: 6-tap horizontal then vertical per sample, 16 multiplies per sample position. Chroma bilinear is lighter (~20 cycles). Adjacent-MB overlap: horizontally adjacent MBs with similar MVs share ~60% of the 21-column reference window. A line buffer can amortise this to ~40 fresh reads/MB instead of 100, but requires per-row pipeline state. WITHOUT overlap exploit: ~250 cycles. WITH overlap: ~150. Allocating 250 (no-overlap case) as the safe target. Note: sub-MB partitions (8x8, 8x16, 16x8, 4x4) may have DIFFERENT MVs per partition, multiplying fetch count. P_Skip with zero MV is essentially free (copy from co-located reference).

deblock.reasoning: 16 edges per MB luma (4 vertical + 4 horizontal internal, plus shared boundary edges). Each edge: read 4+4 samples, compute BS, threshold lookup, conditional 4-tap filter. At ~6 cycles/edge for the full BS→threshold→filter pipeline: 96 cycles for luma. Chroma adds ~16 edges at ~2 cycles/edge: 32 cycles. But luma and chroma edges can pipeline if the filter has 2-cycle throughput. Practical estimate: 100 cycles/MB. The existing h264_deblock_bs and h264_deblock_thresholds are combinational — the cycle cost is in the edge scheduling and sample read/write pattern.

ddr_write.reasoning: Write 384 bytes/MB (256Y + 64Cb + 64Cr) to the current picture in DDR. At 8 bytes/beat: 48 beats minimum. Burst writes amortise bus setup, but arbitration contention with MC reference reads and display line reads adds overhead. 50 cycles allows ~1 cycle/beat overhead for arbitration turnaround.

control_overhead.reasoning: Pipeline stalls, MB-boundary bookkeeping (slice header re-parse at slice boundaries, QP delta application, CBP decode, macroblock address increment). Also includes arbitration pipeline bubbles between DDR requesters.

budget_allocation.verdict: TIGHT BUT FEASIBLE if MC exploits adjacent-MB reference overlap and DDR coalesces to 64-bit beats. Without overlap exploitation, the 250 cycle MC estimate plus 100 cycle deblock leaves only 126 cycles margin for content variation and arbitration contention. Worst-case content (complex MBs, sub-MB partitions, high QP with strong deblocking) could exceed this. The margin is NOT comfortable.

mechanism: Measured from tests/unit/test_stream_path_full_frame_compare.sh with FULL_FRAME_BITSTREAM=tests/fixtures/p3_inter_pred/plex_inter_p16_baseline_624x480_12f.264. Per-stage cycle accounting via stub_busy/fs_wr_reset/fs_swap phase transitions in the Verilator testbench. The aggregate 259 cycles/MB is dominated by decode_stub diagnostic paint (WxH pixels/frame at 1 pixel/cycle) which is NOT a production cost. Production-relevant measured stages are parse_cavlc (~3-4 cycles/MB) and dequant_idct/intra_pred (0 cycles — combinational). MC/deblock/DDR write are NOT IMPLEMENTED and will add significant cost.
